PullRequest.Title: feat: bundle generated code cache into product
PullRequest.Body:
Today main, extension host, shared process, pty host, and agent host repeatedly parses and compiles its startup modules. This change moves that work to build time. CI launches the packaged application once, generates a compile cache for each process, and bundles the caches with the product. At runtime, caches are consumed in portable, read-only mode, so application resources are never modified.

Selective eager compilation is used for the core entry points and a small set of measured startup dependencies, retaining most of the benefit without eagerly compiling every loaded function.

Depends on https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/336697

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The generation gate, tag format, universal merge input, and runtime architecture-prefix check are all explicit in the changed code. The only magnitude uncertainty is the compressed size of the generated cache tree, not whether Intel processes reject it.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Packaged arm64 bytecode cache files and associated download, extraction, filesystem, and disk bytes
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The wasted footprint scales with every generated entry across the five cache kinds; all of those bytes are unusable for every x64 execution of the universal product.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Intel users pay larger download and installation I/O and disk usage while receiving no compile-cache startup benefit.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before the PR the universal package contained no compile-cache payload and Intel launches did not pay to download/install architecture-incompatible cache files.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The universal package is made to contain the arm64-generated cache tree in both merge inputs, so the merged artifact ships that tree even when running as x64.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added line copies the whole `node-compile-cache` directory from whichever macOS input has it into the other. `shouldGenerateNodeCompileCache` generates only for `darwin/arm64`, while runtime matching requires a `${process.version}-${process.arch}-` tag.
Findings.Title: Merge both architecture caches into the universal macOS app
Findings.Impact: Any Intel Mac using the universal archive downloads and installs all five arm64 cache sets, then each Node process finds no x64-prefixed directory and falls back to parsing/compiling as before.
Findings.Evidence: `shouldGenerateNodeCompileCache` returns true for Darwin only when the build target is arm64 (build/lib/nodeCompileCache.ts:32). The new cross-copy operates at the cache root, so the x64 input receives the arm64 tag directories. At runtime `enableNodeCompileCache` looks specifically for `${process.version}-${process.arch}-`; an x64 process therefore cannot consume the copied arm64 entries.
Findings.Recommendation: Generate an x64 cache in the x64 artifact and merge the per-kind architecture tag directories so the universal app contains both arm64 and x64 entries; if x64 generation is unavailable, do not copy/package the unusable arm64 tree in the Intel-only artifact path.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added option is explicitly the boolean all-eager mode, its adjacent comment says it includes inner functions, and the same file declares the bounded moduleIdentifiers form. Generation starts all five cache kinds, so the broader compilation and retained bytecode are directly reachable; only the exact artifact-size increase is unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work and packaged bytecode bytes for inner functions in every startup-loaded module across five processes
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Generation and shipped cache size grow with the total number and size of functions in every module loaded while main, extension host, shared process, pty host, and agent host initialize, rather than with the small measured module set needed for startup.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased product-build CPU plus larger archives, downloads, and installation I/O from bytecode that may never execute.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR the product build did not eagerly compile or package bytecode for these modules; a bounded implementation would eagerly compile only selected measured startup modules and leave other functions lazy.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every inner function in every module loaded by each generated process is eagerly compiled and serialized into the packaged cache.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added generation-only options at lines 78-84 set `eager: true`; the newly added declaration at lines 12-15 exposes `{ moduleIdentifiers: string[] }` as the selective alternative, while app.ts starts all critical Node processes during generation.
Findings.Title: Limit eager compilation to the measured startup modules
Findings.Impact: Every official cache-generating product build performs the extra compilation, and every user downloads and installs the resulting unused bytecode; the cost increases as startup-loaded modules gain functions.
Findings.Evidence: `enableCompileCache` receives generation-only `eager: true`, and the code comment confirms this includes inner functions. Generation explicitly starts the window/extension host, shared process, pty host, and agent host before flushing each cache, so the setting applies across all five startup module graphs. The local API declaration provides a module-identifier allowlist, proving a bounded alternative exists.
Findings.Recommendation: Pass the measured entry points/dependencies through `eager: { moduleIdentifiers: [...] }` and leave all other loaded modules in the default lazy mode before flushing the packaged caches.

Scenarios.Scenario: Normal packaged desktop startup with matching architecture cache
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The main entry synchronously probes the per-kind cache directory and enables Node's read-only portable cache before dynamically importing mainImpl; utility processes do the same before their ESM entry point. Cache-backed module loading remains on each process's startup critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronous existence and directory-name probe, followed by Node compile-cache reads during module loading
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One probe per started process kind; cache data is read on demand for loaded modules.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Processes imported their entry modules directly and parsed/compiled them without probing or reading a packaged compile cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The probe and cache activation happen before the main/utility entry module, directly on startup; matching entries are intended to replace parse/compile CPU.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One cache-directory probe per started Node process, then cache reads scale with modules actually loaded. There are up to five separately keyed process kinds; no per-extension or per-window cache generation occurs at runtime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Main starts first; shared process and renderer-triggered extension host/pty host/agent host may overlap according to existing process startup. Cache directories are separated by kind, so there is no runtime writer contention.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A matching `${node version}-${process.arch}-*` directory enables a portable read-only cache. Warm and cold OS filesystem caches differ only in read latency; missing architecture/version entries cause immediate fallback with no negative cache beyond process lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: entry-point call flow and synchronous filesystem operations are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact startup savings and cache-read latency are not measured in the diff, but the normal-path lookup is bounded and likely offset by avoided compilation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable regression on matching architectures; the bounded lookup serves the intended startup optimization.

Scenarios.Scenario: Official product build generates packaged caches
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After packaging, the new task launches the packaged Electron application and waits for all five process kinds to initialize, flush caches, and write readiness markers before validation and build completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch the packaged Electron product to exercise startup paths and generate cache entries
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One top-level application launch per qualifying packaged target, which transitively starts four utility/extension processes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Packaging did not launch the completed application for compile-cache generation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The packaging task cannot finish until the app exits; a 120-second timeout bounds failure duration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Wait for shared-process readiness, invoke pty-host latency, and start the agent host while the renderer starts the extension host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One startup request per critical process, grouped in one Promise.all.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Normal startup remained lazy for pty/agent paths; packaging did not force this fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All process startups must complete before cache-generation shutdown can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compile and flush generated bytecode, create five readiness files, poll them, enumerate every cache entry, then remove markers
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Five readiness markers; polling checks up to five paths every 50 ms until ready; validation enumerates all emitted entries once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No bytecode cache files or readiness markers were written or validated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Flush, readiness, and validation are mandatory before the product-build task completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The module/function graphs loaded by main, extension host, shared process, pty host, and agent host. Generation validates every emitted cache file across five kind directories.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One packaged Electron subprocess is launched by the build task; after the first window opens, shared process readiness, pty-host IPC, agent-host startup, and window readiness are awaited together. The process-specific cache writes can therefore burst concurrently, while validation is serial by kind.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Generation always deletes the target tree and uses a fresh portable user-data directory, so it is cold every build. Process-kind directories avoid write collisions; readiness markers coordinate completion. There is no reuse across builds.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: generation mode explicitly forces all process starts and sets all-functions eager compilation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number and byte size of compiled functions are not logged, only cache-file counts, so exact build-time and artifact-size growth are unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable eager-work regression: boolean eager mode compiles and packages every inner function in all startup-loaded modules instead of bounding work to selected measured modules.

Scenarios.Scenario: Universal macOS packaging and Intel execution
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The universal build recursively copies the only generated cache root into the other architecture input before makeUniversalApp. At x64 runtime, each process probes for an x64-tagged cache before loading its entry point.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recursively copy the generated node-compile-cache tree from the arm64 app into the x64 universal-merge input
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Every generated cache file across five kind directories is copied once and then included in the universal artifact.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The universal build had no compile-cache tree to copy, merge, sign, or archive.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The synchronous copy and subsequent merge/archive processing are on the universal product-build critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Probe the packaged per-kind directory for an x64 version tag and fall back when only arm64 exists
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One failed probe for each x64 Node process started from the universal app.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Intel startup had no cache probe and no architecture-incompatible cache payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The failed synchronous probe precedes each entry point and yields no parse/compile savings.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Distribute the universal ZIP/DMG containing the arm64-only cache payload to Intel users
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One payload per universal download; bytes scale with all generated arm64 cache entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Universal artifacts did not contain packaged compile-cache bytecode.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds download and installation/extraction bytes before the application can be used.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All cache files emitted for five arm64 process kinds; the entire tree is copied, archived, downloaded, extracted, and stored, but none of it has an x64 runtime tag.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The cross-copy is synchronous and serial before the asynchronous universal merge. Runtime probes occur independently in each started x64 process; there is no coalescing needed because each kind has its own directory.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Darwin generation is gated to arm64. Cross-copy duplicates that arm64 tree into the x64 merge input rather than combining per-architecture tag directories. An Intel process requires an x64 prefix, misses every time, and falls back to compilation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the Darwin arm64-only generation gate, whole-root cross-copy, architecture-bearing cache tags, and runtime process.arch prefix are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The diff does not provide compressed cache size or Intel-user prevalence, so severity is medium rather than high.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable cache-lifecycle regression: Intel users receive all cache bytes but cannot consume any of them.

Scenarios.Scenario: Development/source startup and explicit measurement run
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Development still calls the helper before entry import, but exits cache setup after a bounded filesystem probe. Measurement mode forces critical processes and writes one resource-statistics JSON file per process after readiness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Probe cache directory during development; optionally create measurement directory and synchronously write one JSON record per process
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One probe per process; in explicit measurement mode, up to five small JSON writes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No compile-cache probe or process resource-statistics files were produced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Development probe precedes entry import; measurement writes occur at process readiness and are part of an explicitly instrumented run, not normal startup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most one directory probe and one measurement record per started process kind; measurement payloads contain fixed-shape process statistics.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Measurement forces the same grouped startup fan-out as generation. Each process writes a different kind-named JSON file, avoiding contention.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: VSCODE_DEV disables packaged cache use. Measurement uses any matching packaged cache and records status; missing caches fall back without repeated retries inside a process.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for mechanics, lower for measurement-run prevalence.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Measurement invocation is external and not defined in this repository; normal users do not set the environment flags.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: work is bounded and either negligible in development or explicitly requested by measurement mode.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 17 changed files and relevant startup/build call paths. Submitted two medium-severity findings: unbounded all-functions eager generation inflates build/artifact work, and universal macOS packaging ships an arm64-only cache that Intel processes cannot consume. No concrete shipped-regression fix with an attributable introducing commit was established.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
